source.title: Learning Ability of Interpolating Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies benign overfitting in deep convolutional networks, but it does not test a double-descent curve over model size, epochs, or sample size near an interpolation threshold, nor the other listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper proves that some DCNNs can be made to interpolate while retaining a teacher network's generalization-error bound, and reports test RMSE trends in a sample-size experiment. Neither result measures a double-descent curve. The sample-size experiment is not stated to be near interpolation and changes network depth together with sample size. The cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proves the existence of interpolating DCNNs that keep a teacher network's learning-rate bound. Its only experiment shows test RMSE falling as sample size n grows, with depth tied to n^(1/3). There is no test-error sweep over model size, epochs or samples near an interpolation threshold, and no peak, noise or regularization analysis. Benign overfitting is related to the second descent but does not test any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors give the first learning rates for underparameterized DCNNs without parameter restrictions. They show that deepening such a network can produce interpolating overparameterized DCNNs with the same rates, which theoretically supports benign overfitting. They note that they cannot give necessary and sufficient conditions, and that their rates are not minimax.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops theoretical learning-rate bounds and a layer-deepening construction, with a synthetic-data experiment; it does not use the original double-descent sweeps over model size, epochs, or sample size near interpolation.
record.method_sensitivity: The numerical experiment varies input dimension, and its network depth changes with sample size; no outcome comparison across these settings is numerically reported in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding layers to a non-interpolating teacher DCNN yields an interpolating DCNN with O(n^(1+α)) parameters that keeps the teacher's excess-error bound (Theorems 1 and 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterized interpolating DCNNs can exist that achieve the same learning-rate bound as an underparameterized DCNN (existence of benign overfitting for DCNNs).

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic regression data with depth ⌈n^(1/3)⌉, test RMSE decreases and converges as n increases, and its variance shrinks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For DCNNs with depth co-scaled with sample size, test error falls monotonically with n on simulated data.

record.problems: The theoretical interpolation result is existential and does not characterize a double-descent curve. The numerical experiments use simulated data only; reported test-RMSE values are figure-only, and sample size and depth vary together. The authors note that their rates do not achieve the minimax rate and that they cannot give sufficient and necessary conditions for benign overfitting in DCNNs.

untested.parts: No test error across model sizes or around the interpolation threshold.
No test error over training epochs.
No sample-size sweep near interpolation. Test RMSE falls monotonically with n, but depth is co-scaled and interpolation is not reported.
No risk-versus-capacity curve, and no comparison across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure predicting a peak location.
No variation of noise level or regularization, and no multiple peaks examined.
No reparameterization of complexity to recover a U-shape.

record.verdict_notes: Theoretical paper on benign overfitting. Citing Belkin et al. as background on overparameterization does not amount to a test. The experiment corroborates Theorem 2 (underparameterized networks), not the interpolation result. No row should be linked to a version.

versions.untested_parts: No test-error sweep over model size or interpolation threshold.
No test-error sweep over training epochs or time.
The sample-size experiment does not test increasing data near an interpolation threshold.
No risk-versus-capacity curve across model classes.
No common effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across axes.
No comparison of peak behavior across label-noise levels or regularization choices.
No analysis of whether effective parameter counting turns a second descent into a U-shape.

rows.subject: downsampled DCNN constructed by deepening a teacher DCNN
rows.operation_detail: Add well-defined convolutional layers to construct an interpolating DCNN from a non-interpolating teacher DCNN.
rows.measure: excess generalization error bound, expressed as an L2 error to the regression function
rows.value: the interpolating DCNN retains the teacher's bound (Theorem 1); Theorem 3 gives an explicit high-probability bound for an interpolating DCNN
rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − δ in Theorem 3
rows.note: This is an existence/construction result about interpolating DCNNs, not a measured risk curve as capacity grows.
rows.check: This is an existence theorem about an upper bound, not a measured risk curve. 'observed' is not meaningful for any version. It is fine to keep it as a fits_no_version finding.

relation.reason: The paper addresses the related generalization of interpolating DCNNs without testing or using any listed double-descent version.

tranche.reason: The existence bounds establish possible benign overfitting without testing a double-descent curve. The experiment varies sample size and depth together and does not locate an interpolation threshold.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is supported. Theorem 3 bounds squared L2 error for truncated outputs; the numerical experiment corroborates Theorem 2 and does not establish interpolation.
